newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle futures end lower, feeders up.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle futures end lower, feeders up.

text.p: CME live cattle futures closed mostly lower, pressured by long liquidation by cattle feeding interests, while nearby feeder cattle contracts closed higher.

In live cattle, much of the selling was keyed to ideas $70 per cwt may be the near-term top in cash feedlot markets, traders said. Cash cattle sold at $69.00 last week and although feedlots were pricing cattle at $70 this week, trades at that price were not reported as of early Tuesday afternoon.

"Right now $70 seems to be the top for the next few weeks," said Jim Clarkson, analyst with the brokerage house A & A Inc., "Until we get through that, the board will have trouble getting much above $72."
CME October set a contract high early of 72.35 cents per lb and then slipped back to close down 0.500 cent at 71.725.
Nearby feeder cattle futures held slight gains in reaction to lower CBOT corn futures.
Some of the selling in October live cattle was in anticipation of commission houses transferring long nearby positions to the December contract.
October has risen steadily since April 25 when it traded at 60.00 cents. Also, the 72.35-cent high is the highest futures price since March 1995.
Feeder cattle traded mostly higher, first in reaction to higher cattle futures and later, in response to the downturn in nearby CBOT corn.

Live cattle closed down 0.500 cent to up 0.025 cent with October off 0.500 at 71.725 cents per lb and December was off 0.300 at 67.750. Feeder cattle were up 0.075 to off 0.100 cent with October up 0.075 at 63.225 cents a lb.
